history.summary: No temple or shrine named 'Kandrour Bridge Temple' is documented in web sources after genuine searching. Kandrour Bridge itself is well documented: an 80-m-high, ~280-m-long (sources vary between 255 m and 280 m) road bridge over the Sutlej on NH-88 (some sources say NH-103) at Kandrour village, ~8 km from Bilaspur town; construction began 1959 and finished in 1964/65, and it was once claimed to be Asia's highest bridge. If a small roadside shrine exists near the bridge, it has no web footprint. Coordinates given are those of the Kandrour Bridge itself (approximate) — the shrine's existence and identity need on-the-ground verification. Treat this file as a clearly-flagged placeholder. CSV town 'Bilaspur' corrected to Kandrour (the bridge's village); district remains Bilaspur.

name: Kandrour Bridge Temple
town_description: Kandrour is a village on the Sutlej about 8 km from Bilaspur town, known for the 1965 Kandrour Bridge — once among Asia's highest bridges — and views of Gobind Sagar Lake.

travel.road: On NH-88, ~8 km from Bilaspur bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: March–June, September–November (bridge viewpoint; temple hours unknown)
